headline: Dry, mild weather holds around Mammoth Lakes and across the Sierra through Sunday morning, then a weak storm Sunday night into Monday brings strong ridge winds and high-elevation snow, with a possibly stronger but very uncertain storm Monday night into Tuesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving stays dry and mild across the eastern Sierra, including the Mammoth Lakes area, and western Nevada, with highs in the 50s areawide under cloudy skies. Fog-prone Sierra valleys may see freezing fog form by morning, though the high clouds may limit how much, so use low beams and take care driving in low visibility. No advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday and Saturday stay dry and mild, with highs in the 50s areawide and cloudy skies, and dry weather lasts into Sunday morning. Freezing fog is again possible in Sierra valleys each morning, with about a 20 percent chance around Truckee Friday morning and a better chance Saturday morning. The only exception to the dry weather is a 20 percent or lower chance of light showers near the Oregon border Friday afternoon and evening, and Sierra ridge gusts may pick up Friday but stay under 45 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sierra ridgetop gusts of 45 to 60 mph return Sunday morning, ease during the day, then peak at 60 to 80 mph late Sunday night through Monday morning. A relatively weak low-pressure system Sunday night into Monday brings snow only above about 8,000 feet, with 1 to 4 inches on the highest Sierra peaks, rain lower down of up to 0.4 inch in the Tahoe Basin (locally more along the crest), and just a trace to a couple hundredths of an inch along the Sierra Front and in northeastern California. A colder, potentially stronger storm may arrive late Monday night into Tuesday night, with snow levels above 7,500 feet at first dropping to near 7,000 feet by Tuesday afternoon, but models are split about evenly between a wet and a dry outcome, and recent trends have kept leaning drier.

watch_for: Sierra ridgetop gusts of 60 to 80 mph late Sunday night into Monday morning
Whether the Monday night–Tuesday storm turns wet or mostly misses to the south
Morning freezing fog in Sierra valleys, especially Saturday
confidence: Confidence is high in dry, mild weather through Sunday morning, moderate for the weak Sunday night–Monday system, and low for the Monday night–Tuesday storm, which is more than five days out with models split on how wet it will be.
